title: Holy Fire in the Warsaw Ghetto
hookLine: Rabbi Kalonymus Shapira gave Hasidic sermons in the Warsaw ghetto; his manuscript survived buried
carry: torah study kept the holy spark alive
tomorrow: where does God go to weep?

lines: ONE MATCH, AND THE WALLS COME BACK.
cards: Strike a match in a dark room and the room changes size. One small flame, and the walls come back.

A note before today's story, for anyone listening with children: it takes place during the Holocaust, and it's told gently. The answer to the question is a rabbi named Kalonymus Kalman Shapira, the rebbe of Piaseczno.
Shut inside the Warsaw ghetto with his community, he kept teaching. On Shabbat and on festivals he gave Hasidic talks on the Torah, and he wrote them down.

teach.b: Those talks are a record of a teacher trying to hold his people's faith while the world fell apart around them. Readers notice that as things grow darker, the questions in them grow harder, and he doesn't hide them.
He doesn't claim to know why. What he keeps doing is teaching: how to pray when you can't, how to keep the spark of the soul alive when everything outside is trying to put it out.
Near the end, his pages were hidden away and buried in the ground. He did not survive the war.

After it, the pages were found, and they were published under the name Esh Kodesh, Holy Fire. So who keeps teaching when every light goes out? Someone who knew the lesson might never be read, and wrote it anyway.
He was writing for the people in front of him that week, and for whoever might come after. Notice the senses in the story: paper, ink, a buried container, earth, and then a book opened in daylight.

teach.h: TORAH STUDY KEPT THE HOLY SPARK ALIVE.
teach.b: That's why today's practice is small and physical. A flame doesn't explain the darkness. It just refuses to let the darkness be the only thing in the room.

how: Esh Kodesh, Rabbi Kalonymus Kalman Shapira's ghetto sermons, is studied as Torah and as testimony, and on Yom HaShoah and other days of remembrance Jews light memorial candles for those who were murdered.

games.q: what does “teaching in the dark” mean?
o: talks given in the ghetto, buried, and found after the war
lessons held at night because the day was for working
the teaching that God is hidden and can never be known

games.q: a light kept in the dark — tap the pairs.

s: Rabbi Shapira's talks claim to explain why the suffering happened
he doesn't claim to know why; he keeps teaching how to hold on.
his pages survived buried in the ground
found after the war and published as Esh Kodesh, Holy Fire.
Rabbi Shapira escaped and published the book himself
he did not survive the war; the pages were found and published after it.

games.q: your cousin leads a small study group that's down to three people, and she wonders if it's worth teaching at all. what does teaching in the dark suggest?
o: keep teaching; a lesson can outlive the moment it's given in.
stop until more people come; teaching only works with a crowd.
teach only if they can promise it will make a difference.
games.why: Rabbi Shapira taught not knowing if anyone would read his words. they were buried, found, and are studied today as Esh Kodesh.

practice: Dim the lights if you can. Light a candle, or turn on one small light, even a phone screen turned low, and look at it for the sit.
Let it stand for faith kept in the dark, and hold in mind, quietly, the people who kept teaching when no one knew if anyone would ever read it.
